title: Multitask Mayhem: Unveiling and Mitigating Safety Gaps in LLMs Fine-tuning

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model responses and computing Attack Success Rate (ASR) using a GPT-4o judge on prompts from the CrowS-Pairs dataset, which contains sentence pairs differing in a single bias aspect to evaluate social biases in masked language models.

bias_targets.target: Bias and implicit hate speech against minority groups
bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of fine-tuned models on prompts sourced from the Toxigen dataset, which includes toxic and benign statements targeting 13 different minority groups.

Testing models with manually crafted adversarial prompts requesting offensive content, mockery of cultural traditions, or the use of racial stereotypes, and evaluating whether the model complies or refuses.
Evaluating model responses to multiple-choice classification prompts that associate harmful stereotypes (e.g., 'terrorists') with specific religious identities (e.g., Muslim vs. Jew).

Testing models with multiple-choice classification prompts that invoke negative gender stereotypes (e.g., associating a specific gender with being 'too sensitive') and measuring the model's willingness to answer.
Prompting the model to generate discriminatory remarks, slurs, or homophobic content, and using a GPT-4o judge to assess whether the safety guardrails successfully reject the request.
